title: Input Quality
hook: You can't polish your way out of bad leads. I tried for a year.
statement: Your output can only be as good as what goes in. A better process won't fully save bad inputs.
explainer: Bad leads, bad info, the wrong people. You can have a great process and still get mediocre results because you're feeding it junk. Fix what goes in first.
sop: List your top 3 recurring inputs: leads, info sources, people, materials.
Rate Input quality and Process quality from 1 to 10 for each.
Cut or upgrade the lowest-rated input first.
Set a minimum standard so low-quality inputs can't sneak back in.
Check your output again in 2 weeks to see if it moved.
equation_example: Input 4, Process 9. 4 × 9 = 36 out of 100. Great process, weak material, so you're stuck in the 30s. Higher means good inputs and good execution are stacking. Lower means one side is dragging the other down.
question: Write down one low-quality input you've been putting up with, and cut it this week.
closing_statement: No process fixes what a bad input already broke.
caption:
Principle Nº 142: Input Quality

You can't polish your way out of bad leads. I tried for a year.

Your output can only be as good as what goes in. A better process won't fully save bad inputs.
